summary_paraphrase: Banzi and Gogo, the grandmother, love her garden and its bees; after a few days away they find the bees and flowers gone. Gogo promises a magic trick: plant new sunflowers, leave out water and call the bees with a chant. For a week nothing seems to happen, while the pictures show the seeds rooting and sprouting under the soil; then the flowers bloom and the bees return.

beats.function: the garden, the bees and the buzzing call-and-answer; goodbye to the bees
the trick: plant seeds, leave water, chant
a week of waiting; the text says nothing happens while the picture shows roots then shoots
grandmother and child laugh and dance

characters.name: Banzi
characters.age: young child (collage figure; age and gender not stated)
characters.change: learns, by waiting and tending, how the bees come back
characters.tension_source: the empty garden and the waiting

characters.name: Gogo
characters.desire: to bring the bees back for Banzi
characters.relation_to_protagonist: grandmother; supplies the plan framed as a magic trick

characters.name: the bees
characters.relation_to_protagonist: loved creatures; answer the buzzing; their absence is the problem

humor_notes: Gentle: the bees answering the buzz; the picture contradicting 'nothing yet' twice gives the listener a knowing, slightly comic advantage.

repetition.description: A buzzing sound call-and-answer between Banzi, Gogo and the bees
repetition.why: a sound word small listeners can say along; it also establishes what is lost when the bees go

repetition.description: Gogo's calling chant, repeated twice inside itself, then echoed by Banzi in a whisper with one word changed
repetition.why: the child echoes the adult, modelling how a listener can join

repetition.description: The same two-word report that nothing has happened yet, on two consecutive spreads
repetition.why: the words stay still while the pictures move (roots, then shoots), so the turn becomes a game of seeing more than the characters

notes: OBSERVED: torn-paper and found-material collage (street maps, newspaper, cardboard) with figures built from flat shapes; characters have no faces.
OBSERVED: on spreads 10-11 a cut-away of the soil shows the seeds growing roots and then shoots while the text twice says nothing has happened: the picture tells the reader first.
INFERRED: spread 4 draws the garden brown and withered with fallen petals, so the picture shows the flowers died, while the text says they disappeared.
OBSERVED: the final spread shows full sunflowers, which explains the bees' return without the text naming the cause.
OBSERVED: spreads 5-6 drop the background entirely: figures and objects on blank paper for the problem and the plan.

strengths: a sound refrain to say along
the picture runs ahead of the text during the wait, rewarding close looking
a real-world cause (flowers and water bring bees) framed as play
calm, unhurried waiting shown across several spreads
weaknesses: the child does what the adult says; the plan and the chant both come from Gogo
framing a natural process as 'magic' leaves the cause unstated for a child who does not read the pictures closely
faceless collage figures make feeling depend on gesture alone

anti_patterns.note: Banzi follows Gogo's plan and echoes her chant; the child does not originate the solution (INFERRED)

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Gentle loss (bees gone, flowers withered) resolved by patient care. 'Magic trick' framing is playful; a retelling could name the real cause. Bees shown as friendly; no stinging or handling.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters

causal_chain.cause: they go away for a few days
causal_chain.effect: the bees and flowers are gone
they plant seeds, leave water, chant
seeds root and sprout (shown, not said)

ending.last_page_move: grandmother and child dance among the bees

craft.writer_note: A learning tale can hide the real cause in plain sight (flowers and water bring bees) and let the 'magic' frame carry the waiting. In text-only tales the real cause must be said once.
